The Petitioner has submitted that the delay in commissioning the sub-station is due to such scope modification and is not attributable to the Petitioner. 46. The Petitioner has further submitted that, with regard to land acquisition, continuous follow-up was undertaken with the concerned authorities and the Investment Approval was obtained after finalisation of DPR based on land particulars. The Petitioner has submitted that the delay in land acquisition, RoW issues, and APIIC approvals was due to factors beyond its control, and that it has placed necessary correspondence and joint inspections on record. The Petitioner has also submitted that the landowner objections arose subsequently and it took appropriate action thereafter. Further, the Petitioner has submitted that the Model Code of Conduct during the General Elections also affected work progress due to constraints in manpower and administrative support. Accordingly, the Petitioner has submitted that the delay in commissioning the assets was beyond its control and should be dealt with in accordance with the applicable Tariff Regulations. 51. However, the Petitioner has not furnished any detailed activity-wise analysis demonstrating the manner and extent to which the revised scope affected the scheduled dated 09.02.2024, the subsequent process undertaken by the District Administration to resolve compensation/ROW issues, and continued obstruction at certain locations. However, the Petitioner's claim for condonation of the entire 401-day period cannot be accepted merely on the ground that ROW issues persisted during that period. The period of delay must be examined with reference to the specific events that actually prevented execution of the works and the steps the Petitioner took to resolve such issues. - (iv) The Petitioner continued to pursue the matter with the District Administration, including meetings, site inspections and determination of compensation. The period from 16.08.2024 to 26.09.2024, during which the matter was under active consideration of the District Administration and the compensation was determined and directed to be deposited, is considered beyond the - (vi) The Petitioner has claimed condonation of 164 days from 05.09.2024 to 15.02.2025 on account of ROW issues at Location Nos. 23/1 to 29/0 arising from objections raised by the landowners and the consequent administrative proceedings for resolution of the compensation dispute. The submissions of the Petitioner have been considered. It is noted that the time overrun up to 17.01.2025 has already been condoned on account of ROW issues at Location Nos. 17/1, 17/5 and 17/6. Therefore, the period from 05.09.2024 to 17.01.2025 59. We observed that the issue relating to APIIC land was identified by the Petitioner on 24.04.2023 itself. Although APIIC subsequently declined to issue the NOC for construction through its land, the Petitioner has not established that the entire period from 24.04.2023 to 12.10.2023 was beyond its control. The Petitioner was aware of the land-related constraint and could have explored and finalised an alternative alignment. Further, the record indicates that the Petitioner made the formal request for NOC only in July 2023 and finalised the revised alignment on 12.10.2023 after APIIC's rejection dated 11.09.2023. The Petitioner has also not demonstrated, with adequate documentary evidence, the specific activities undertaken during the intervening period or the extent to which each delay period was directly attributable to APIIC. Accordingly, the claimed delay of 172 days from 24.04.2023 to 12.10.2023 cannot be treated in its entirety as an 64. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner. The Petitioner stated that the issues were resolved through discussions with the district administration and work resumed thereafter. However, the Petitioner has not submitted sufficient evidence to establish that the said events completely prevented the Petitioner from carrying out construction activities at other available locations during the claimed period. 74. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner. The stoppage of work arose from a localised incident of theft in the vicinity of the work site and the consequential investigation by the local police. Although the movement of the labourers was restricted for two days, the Petitioner has not established that the said incident falls within the scope of an uncontrollable factor warranting condonation of time overrun under to furnish certain information.
